snippet: Before you arrive, keep your OSHC policy documents. The PDS explains the policy. The MBS is a government fee list used as a reference for many medical services. A clinic may charge more than the MBS fee, so a gap may apply. Check the official policy information before you book or pay.

Before you travel, save your OSHC details and know where to find the PDS. If you visit a clinic, ask about the fee and billing before the appointment. Keep any invoice or receipt. A refund or benefit depends on the service and policy, so check the official information instead of guessing.

New to OSHC? Learn these words first. MBS is a fee schedule used as a reference for medical services. A gap is the amount left between a charge and a benefit. An invoice shows what the provider charged. For ambulance, scans, outpatient care, or other services, check the PDS and ask the insurer when you are unsure.
